explanation: The OK sign (thumb and forefinger circle) is understood in Spain the same way as in most of Western Europe — meaning 'fine', 'good', or 'perfect' — and does not carry the vulgar meaning it has in Brazil, Turkey, or parts of the Middle East. A handful of travel-advice lists lump Spain in with Latin America on this gesture, but more detailed sources specifically note Spain (and Portugal) as an exception where it isn't considered offensive.
local_tip: Feel free to use the OK sign to mean 'all good' or 'perfect' — it's not read as vulgar in Spain the way it can be in Brazil or Turkey.

also_check.note: The same gesture is a well-known vulgar insult, famously causing embarrassment for foreign visitors who used it unknowingly.
